name: Google Workspace
scope_notes: Context-Aware Access requires eligible Workspace/Cloud Identity editions. User policy coverage does not establish protection of DWD service accounts.

controls.name: App access control: Blocked / Limited / Specific Google data / Trusted
controls.what: Per OAuth app, blocks it, limits it to unrestricted services, or limits it to admin-chosen scopes.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Third-Party App Access
controls.quote: Can request data access only to scopes that you specify when configuring the app.

controls.name: Unconfigured third-party apps
controls.what: Blocks Sign in with Google to apps the admin has not configured, or allows only basic-profile requests.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Settings > Unconfigured third-party apps
controls.quote: Users can't sign in with Google to any third-party apps and websites until you configure those apps and sites

controls.name: Allow users to request access to unconfigured third-party apps
controls.what: Users blocked from an unconfigured app can request it; admins review the request.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Settings
controls.quote: check the Allow users to request access to unconfigured third-party apps box.

controls.name: Google services: Restricted
controls.what: Marks a Workspace service so only Trusted or Specific-data apps can reach its data.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Google Services
controls.quote: Only internal and third-party apps configured with a Trusted or Specific Google data access setting can access data.

controls.name: Restrict high-risk OAuth scopes
controls.what: For Gmail, Drive, Docs and Chat, blocks a predefined list of high-risk scopes for non-trusted apps.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Google Services
controls.quote: Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, and Chat can also restrict access to a predefined list of high-risk OAuth scopes.

controls.name: Trust internal apps
controls.what: When checked, all internal apps can reach restricted APIs; leaving it off keeps internal apps under the same restrictions.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Settings
controls.quote: To allow API access for all internal apps, check the Trust internal apps box.

controls.name: Access levels for OAuth apps (Context-Aware Access)
controls.what: Requires IP, location, device or identity conditions when users sign in to OAuth apps with Google; checked at sign-in only.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Context-Aware Access > General Settings > Access levels for OAuth apps
controls.plan: Frontline, Enterprise, Education, Enterprise Essentials Plus, Cloud Identity Premium
controls.quote: Context-Aware Access rules are applied only when a user signs in through Google.

controls.name: Context-Aware Access for Workspace APIs
controls.what: Applies CAA access levels to first- and third-party apps reaching Workspace core data through APIs.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Context-Aware Access
controls.plan: Enterprise Standard/Plus, Education Standard/Plus, Cloud Identity Premium
controls.quote: Admins can now use context-aware access to block users' access to Workspace Applications

controls.name: Google Cloud session control
controls.what: Forces reauthentication every 1-24 hours for apps holding user grants to Google Cloud scopes, similar to revoking their refresh tokens.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Google Cloud session control
controls.quote: analogous to what would happen if an admin revoked the refresh tokens for that application.

controls.name: Manage Domain Wide Delegation
controls.what: Super admins authorize each service account or OAuth client ID with an explicit scope list; editing scopes or deleting the client stops access.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Domain Wide Delegation
controls.quote: add each scope that the application can access (should be appropriately narrow).

controls.name: Multi-party approval for domain-wide delegation
controls.what: When enabled, adding, editing or deleting a DWD client needs a second super admin's approval.
controls.quote: requires approval from another super admin.

controls.name: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation / iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
controls.what: Org policy that blocks creation of user-managed service account keys used to sign DWD JWTs.
controls.quote: If your organization was created on or after May 3, 2024, this constraint is enforced by default.

controls.name: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload
controls.what: Org policy that blocks uploading external public keys to service accounts.
controls.quote: When this constraint is set, users cannot upload public keys to service accounts in projects affected by the constraint.

controls.name: iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours
controls.what: Org policy that sets a maximum lifetime for new service account keys, which otherwise never expire.
controls.quote: A service account key lets you authenticate a request as a service account. By default, service account keys never expire.

controls.name: iam.disableServiceAccountCreation
controls.what: Org policy that blocks creating new service accounts.
controls.setting: Google Cloud Organization Policy (constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountCreation or managed variant)
controls.quote: disable the creation of new service accounts

controls.name: Service account impersonation IAM (Service Account Token Creator)
controls.what: Only principals granted impersonation roles on the service account can mint tokens or sign JWTs as it.
controls.setting: Google Cloud IAM on the service account
controls.quote: Only authenticated principals with the appropriate permissions can impersonate service accounts.

controls_unknown: Whether Workspace Context-Aware Access or third-party app access settings apply to domain-wide delegation service account calls; the DWD page does not say.
Edition requirement for multi-party approval on DWD changes.
No per-DWD-client IP restriction found in Workspace docs; absence not stated by Google.
Default of 'Trust internal apps' not stated on the fetched page.
Exact UI path for applying CAA to Workspace APIs; the 2023 update links to help articles without naming the setting.

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 user bearer tokens; service-account signed JWT exchange. Domain-wide delegation (DWD) enables approved user impersonation.

federation.details: Google documents WIF → service account → IAM signJwt → OAuth token for DWD. Workspace scopes/admin delegation remain separate requirements.

ip_restriction.boundary: Context-Aware Access (eligible editions) can apply IP/device/location access levels to internal and third-party OAuth apps, checked when the user signs in through Google; active sessions are not re-evaluated. Its documentation excludes service-account API access.

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens stay valid until revoked, but expire after six months unused, after 7 days for external apps in Testing status, on Google Cloud session-length limits, or when the 100-per-client limit is exceeded.

administration.summary: Approve/block third-party OAuth apps and scopes; restrict DWD scopes; control service-account IAM and key creation.
administration.conditions: Context-Aware Access requires eligible Workspace/Cloud Identity editions. User policy coverage does not establish protection of DWD service accounts.

sso.details: OAuth apps can be held to Context-Aware Access levels at Google sign-in, and Workspace services can apply Context-Aware Access to API access (Enterprise, Education Standard/Plus, Frontline, Cloud Identity Premium).

offboard.details: Suspending a user resets their sign-in cookies and OAuth tokens.

inventory.details: Admin console App access control shows an Accessed apps list with user counts; active tokens are listed only per user per app on the user's Security page.

sso.ui: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Context-Aware Access > Assign access levels to apps > (app) Assign; Policy settings: check "Block other apps from accessing the selected apps via APIs, if access levels aren't met"

usage.ui: Admin console > Reporting > Audit and investigation > OAuth log events; filter by app / client ID

reads.ui: OAuth log events (Event = activity, API method / Number of response bytes); Gmail: Reporting > Audit and investigation > Gmail log events

offboard.ui: Admin console > Directory > Users > (user) > More options > Suspend user

token_format.notes: Opaque bearer tokens. GitHub scans google_oauth_access_token, google_oauth_refresh_token, google_oauth_client_secret; Google docs fetched give no prefix/regex.

log_sources.notes: App access control changes (blocked/trusted apps). 6 months.

anomaly_cues: authorize for a client_id never seen in the domain with Gmail/Drive scopes
activity events with high num_response_bytes from GMAIL or DRIVE product_bucket right after authorize
Token activity from ipAddress/ASN not used by the user's interactive logins
Use continuing after revoke (lag aside) suggests a second grant or other client
deny events with SCOPE_BLOCK showing an attacker probing scopes

containment.steps: Admin: Directory API tokens.delete for user+clientId; add the app to the blocked list (ADD_TO_BLOCKED_OAUTH2_APPS); user/app: POST token to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke; reset user if account compromised.
containment.notes: Revoking an access token also revokes its refresh token; tokens.delete removes all access tokens for that user+app.

containment.steps: Delete or disable the key; remove the client ID from domain-wide delegation; disable the service account to stop issued short-lived credentials; review and remove IAM bindings.
